items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: And I wrote it for Joe Romano, a great alto

ctx.x: Yes, the one I was listening to last night, I think it was Clay playing on it. And he had a lot of space, as did the tenor player who followed him.
Yeah, you know I wrote a chart for Buddy, we were in Boston at Lenny’s on the Turnpike. It was “God Bless the Child.” And I wrote it for Joe Romano, a great alto

player. You probably knew Joe, I’m sure. And so I wrote it in a day, because he wanted it the next night. And I brought it in and I really was pleased with it. And you know, in the second chorus there was nothing except the rhythm section and Joe, all that nice space. Because most soloists don’t like backgrounds underneath them. They want that freedom to take it wherever they want to go. And then that night after the gig Buddy says, “Fill that in, I don’t like that, it’s too much open space, fill that in.” And he…
